## SortDirection

```typescript
type SortDirection = "ascending" | "descending"
```

Which way a column is sorted, or not.

## SortableThProps

```typescript
interface SortableThProps extends Omit<ThHTMLAttributes<HTMLTableCellElement>, "onClick" | "aria-sort">
```

What a `SortableTh` takes.

| Member | Kind | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `children` | field | `ReactNode` | The heading. |
| `direction` | field | `SortDirection` | How this column is currently sorted, or `undefined` when the table is sorted by some other column. |
| `onSort` | field | `(direction: SortDirection) => void` | Asked to sort by this column. Gets the direction to go to. |
| `numeric` | field | `boolean` | Right-align and use tabular figures. |

## SortableTh

```typescript
function SortableTh({ children, direction, onSort, numeric = false, className, ...rest }: SortableThProps)
```

A column heading you can sort by.

`aria-sort` goes on the `th` and nowhere else, which is what a
screen reader reads; the arrow is `aria-hidden` so the state is
not announced twice. Hand-rolled versions usually do the reverse —
an arrow glyph with no `aria-sort` — and the sort is then
invisible to the people most reliant on being told.

The button fills the cell so the whole heading is the target
rather than a word inside it.

**Also** [`SortableThProps`](/docs/sdk/ui-react/reference-the-table#sortablethprops).
